primary.note: The one saturated color. Blend of TMDB's historical green and an Amazon redesign concept seen on Dribbble. Same value as `success`.

primaryLightest.note: Type set on a green field.

accent.note: The second green on a screen that already has a primary one: link hover, secondary button.

secondary.note: The only cool hue in the palette. A ground behind bright content.

plex.note: Plex's brand orange, not a Sensorr color. Present so a Plex affordance looks like Plex.

error.note: A broken policy, a destructive button, a failed job.

warning.note: A job that ran but did not finish its work.

text.note: The body reading color in dark mode. `textLight` through `textLightest` run up to 98%, closer to the surface they contrast with.

gray.note: The layer stack. `white` is the page, `grayLightest`/`grayLighter`/`grayLight` are panels on it, `gray` is a filled chip, `grayDark`/`grayDarker`/`grayDarkest` are borders in three states. The project's own `gray-900` to `gray-50` scale, dark to light.

whitePure.note: One of the two colors that never invert between modes. Use when you need actual white regardless of mode.

h1.purpose: Page title, one per screen. Raleway 800 at scale step 0.

h3.purpose: Sub-section, and the /design gallery stage title.

h4.purpose: Scale step 3 of the heading ramp.

h5.purpose: Scale step 4 of the heading ramp.

h6.purpose: Scale step 5 of the heading ramp, the smallest heading.

label.purpose: A field's name, in the heading face. A field label is a small heading.

body.purpose: The default, set on `body` in global.ts. Line-height 1.2.

body-long.purpose: Same face at reading line-height 1.5, for anything longer than a line: inputs, overviews, Warning subtitles.

button.purpose: Button text. Semibold, one step below body, line-height reset to 1 so height comes from padding.

caption.purpose: A poster's year and genre line.

mono.purpose: Badge labels and transition pills. Fira Code marks a value the machine produced or parsed.

shadows.name: poster-glow
shadows.purpose: The single intentional shadow in the system, at libs/ui/src/elements/Entity/Poster/Poster.tsx:483. A 30px blur with no spread, tinted with the poster's own most chromatic color. Reads as a lamp behind the artwork, not a drop shadow.

shadows.name: range-focus-ring
shadows.purpose: The Range thumb at rest, libs/ui/src/inputs/Range/Range.tsx:183. Spread only, zero blur: a ring, not a shadow. Grows to 8px on hover and 14px while dragging.

motion.name: appear
motion.purpose: The house transition, 9 occurrences. Anything appearing or leaving.

motion.name: field
motion.purpose: Inputs, selects and textareas. Fast, because it answers a keystroke.

motion.name: control
motion.value: color 200ms ease-in-out, background-color 200ms ease-in-out, border-color 200ms ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Buttons. All three properties move together so a button never appears to change shape.

motion.name: nav
motion.purpose: Web navigation items rising from 0.33 to 0.66 on hover.

motion.name: palette-bleed
motion.purpose: The Shadow atom, the slowest thing in the app: a poster's color bleeding into the page.

motion.name: view-transition
motion.purpose: Route changes through the View Transitions API. Five named transitions in modules.css: fade, top, forward, backward, and root explicitly set to animation: none.

narrative.overview:
Not a slogan invented for this document. It is the line the product already says about itself, in seven places, and spelled out in full in apps/web/src/pages/KeepInTouch/KeepInTouch.tsx:155: "A Friendly Digital Video Recorder. Think VCR but in modern times." Every screen answers to that sentence.

A VCR is a machine you program once and then trust. Sensorr's subject is the movie and its release: a policy sorts candidate releases into require, prefer and avoid groups, and the interface's real job is to show what that policy did - which axis held, which one broke, what a swap would cost. The Proposal screen is where the product is most itself: five axes (resolution, source, encoding, dub, language) rendered as before-after pills, green when the policy still holds, red when it breaks. Followed, KeepInTouch, Person and Calendar are discovery paths - the part Radarr does not have - but they feed the wishlist; they are not the subject.

So the surface is dense and instrumented rather than spacious. A poster carries up to six badges. A row of metadata is monospaced because it is data, not prose. The chrome is near-black so the posters carry the color, and the one saturated green is reserved for the thing the machine decided. Emoji do the work of an icon set: there is no icon font and no icon package in libs/ui.
keyCharacteristics: Instrumented: every state a job can be in has a badge, and every badge says which.
Discreet: chrome recedes to near-black, the artwork is the color.
Dense: information per screen is high on purpose; a library is a wall of posters.
Detailed: five-axis diffs, superscript policy ranks, byte-exact sizes.
Fine: 1px borders, 0.25em radii, no ornament above the data.
UX-friendly: every control says its state before you touch it.

rules.name: The Poster Paints the Screen Rule
rules.body: Sensorr does not pick accent colors for content - it takes them from the artwork at runtime. libs/palette/ loads the poster into a canvas, ships the pixels to a Web Worker, and gets back five values: backgroundColor, color, alternativeColor, accentColor and colorfulColor. The worker pairs the dominant color with every other extracted color, keeps only pairs above a contrast threshold, and lightens or darkens the partner until the pair reaches 4.5:1 - so a palette taken from a poster is WCAG-corrected before it is ever painted. When a surface shows one movie, the theme's neutrals are the frame and the poster's palette is the content. Do not hardcode an accent for a movie-scoped surface.

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: primary and success are the same hsla(154, 99%, 41%, 1). Green therefore always means the system says yes: this is on, this is kept, this held. Never reach for green because a surface needs a color.

rules.name: The Declared-and-Unreachable Light Mode Rule
rules.body: libs/theme/src/lib/theme/colors.ts:75-101 defines a complete 27-line light palette, and colors.ts:144 registers it as modes.light. index.ts:11-14 sets initialColorModeName: 'dark' and useColorSchemeMediaQuery: false, and nothing in the application calls setColorMode or useColorMode - the only references to colorMode anywhere in apps/ and libs/ are reads. The light palette is therefore dead code that stays correct: it is documented debt, not a feature. Keep it consistent when you add a color, but do not describe Sensorr as having a light theme, and do not build a toggle without deciding first whether the light palette is still wanted.

rules.name: The Monospace-Means-Machine Rule
rules.body: Fira Code is never a stylistic choice. It marks a value the machine produced or parsed: a release name, an axis value, a resolution, a size, a count, a policy rank. If a human wrote the string, it is Open Sans. If a parser produced it, it is Fira Code.

rules.name: The No Free Sizes Rule
rules.body: Every font size is an index into one thirteen-step scale, and that same scale is the spacing scale. fontSize: 5 and paddingY: 5 are the same 0.875em. Never write a font size as a literal; take the nearest step.

rules.name: The No Shadow Rule
rules.body: A new surface gets a tonal step and a 1px border. If you find yourself reaching for box-shadow to separate two things, the two things need different gray* values instead. The only sanctioned exceptions are a color taken from artwork (the poster glow) and a spread-only focus halo.

rules.name: The Pill-Is-A-State Rule
rules.body: Anything fully rounded is read-only information about state: a wishlist badge, a policy axis, a tag. Anything with a 0.25em corner is something you can press. Do not round an action into a pill.

dos: Do take colors from libs/theme/src/lib/theme/colors.ts by token name. The literal hsl(0, 0%, 100%) in Button.tsx and the hsl(0, 0%, 10%) family beside it are pre-existing exceptions, not a pattern to copy.
Do use the shared scale for both spacing and type, remembering it runs descending - 12 is zero and 0 is 2em.
Do let usePalette color anything scoped to one movie, and keep the theme's neutrals as the frame around it.
Do separate surfaces with a tonal step plus a 1px grayDark border.
Do reach for Badge for a state, Tag for a link, Button for an action.
Do put machine-produced strings in the monospace face and human-written strings in the body face.
Do add a variant by adding a named export to the component's *.stories.tsx and checking it at /design/:stage/:component while yarn web runs.
Do run node tools/docs/check-design.mjs after editing libs/theme or DESIGN.md's frontmatter.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow. The system is flat; use a tonal step.
Don't use green for anything other than "the system says yes". primary and success are the same value, and that identity is the meaning.
Don't round an action into a pill, or square off a state badge.
Don't fill or shadow an input to show focus - move border-color and nothing else.
Don't write a font size, a padding or a margin as a raw value; take a scale step.
Don't assume light mode works. The light palette is declared and unreachable; see the named rule in Colors.
Don't introduce an icon library. Emoji and inline SVG are the icon set, and the font stacks are built around that.
Don't change primary to fix the contrast gap. That is a brand decision, not a styling one.
